newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Top Philippine judge says Supreme Court not guilty.
newsitem.headline: Top Philippine judge says Supreme Court not guilty.

text.p: The Chief Justice of the Philippines has attacked a recent spate of articles charging the Supreme Court with being corrupt, saying the allegations were based on little more than rumour and innuendo.

The country's top court has come under the spotlight after several controversial decisions in commercial cases, followed by accusations that some judgements were inconsistent and possibly swayed by bribes.

"(The reports are) for the most part hearsay, gossip, calumny, insult, directed against people whose credentials are, on record, of superior quality," Chief Justice Andres Narvasa told the annual convention of Philippine judges on Thursday.
In one recent case, the Supreme Court refused to allow a foreign company to buy one of Manila's leading hotels on the grounds that it was a national asset, even though it made the highest bid.
In another case, a local firm was allowed to virtually copy the trademark of a well known U.S. brand of jeans.
Narvasa insisted that the Supreme Court took its bearings from the constitution and the law.
"It is not free to blaze new trials and adopt principles other than those laid down by constitutional and statutory precepts."
He warned judges that they may come under attack for their decisions.

"But let us not be moved by fickle and temporary expressions of passion and prejudice, the tirades of demagogues and spiteful writers, or the whispered calumnies of disgruntled litigants or lawyers or yield to the temptation to do what is popular, rather than what is right."
